summary: On the default 60-px strip the port is visually indistinguishable from the original — same rainbow head hue map, same head position at every dumped time, same wrap behaviour, steady for 240 s — differing only in that its comet tail is 9 px instead of 10 (~10% dimmer); off the default rig the divergence grows because the original's tail is a FIXED 10 pixels while the port's is 15% of the pixel count.
observations: Both sides render a single rainbow 'comet': a bright head pixel with a linearly-fading tail behind it, sweeping left-to-right along the strip and restarting at pixel 0. One regime only — a 240 s / 2 fps survey (survey-long) shows the identical sawtooth waterfall for both sides end to end, with no mode rotation, palette walk, or drift.

Head position is IDENTICAL on both sides at every time checked. dump-a (60 px, 20 fps): head index t=1 s -> 9/9, t=2 s -> 18/18, t=4 s -> 37/37, t=6 s -> 55/55, t=7.95 s -> 13/13 (orig/port). Speed 9.25 px/s, full 60-px traverse every ~6.5 s.
Phase does NOT drift: at t=120/125/130/139 s (label 'late', --skip 120) the head is still at the same index on both sides (19, wrap, 51, 13).

Both sides are time-based, not frame-stepped: head displacement measured from --dump at t=1 s and t=5 s gives 9.00 px/s at --fps 10 and 9.25 px/s at --fps 20 and --fps 40, identical on orig and port (labels fps-10/fps-20/fps-40).

TAIL LENGTH (default 60-px rig): original lights 10 px, port lights 9 px, on every frame checked over 0-140 s. Exact per-pixel values at t=4 s, head at index 37: orig 37:(0,75,252) 36:(0,90,227) 35:(0,100,201) 34:(0,105,176) 33:(0,105,150) 32:(0,100,125) 31:(0,89,99) 30:(0,74,74) 29:(0,48,43) 28:(0,23,18); port 37:(0,75,252) 36:(0,89,224) 35:(0,97,195) 34:(0,100,167) 33:(0,97,139) 32:(0,88,110) 31:(0,74,82) 30:(0,54,54) 29:(0,25,23). The head pixel is byte-identical; the fade ramp is linear on both sides but reaches zero at offset 10 on the original vs offset 9 on the port (per-pixel step 25.4 vs 28.3 out of 252).

Consequence of the short tail: meanBrightness avg 10.6 (orig) vs 9.5 (port) over the 6 s baseline, 10.5 vs 9.5 over the late window; meanR/G/B max 23 vs 21. Both sides brightnessTrend 'steady', zeroMotionFrames 1 (baseline) / 0 (late), motion avg 1.9 vs 1.9. Untouched per-channel difference: mean 1.1/255, max 25/255 across all dump-a frames.

HUE MAP IS EXACT. At every tail offset the two sides' RGB triples are the same hue with different value (e.g. px 30 orig (0,74,74) vs port (0,54,54); px 33 orig (0,105,150) G/B ratio 0.700 vs port (0,97,139) ratio 0.698). Head colour cycles red -> yellow -> green -> cyan -> blue -> magenta -> red across one traverse on both sides.

WRAP BEHAVIOUR IDENTICAL (label 'wrap', dumps 6.40-6.60 s at 20 fps): the tail does not wrap around the strip end. At t=6.55 s both sides show a fresh head at pixel 0 (orig 243/0/0, port 242/0/0) while the previous tail is still fading at pixels 51-59, and it decays in place rather than wrapping to the far end.

RIG-SCALING DIVERGENCE (structural, seen only via rig override). The original's tail is a FIXED absolute 10 pixels at every rig size; the port's is ~15% of the pixel count. Measured lit-pixel counts at t=3 s: 12 px -> orig 10, port 2; 60 px -> orig 10, port 9; 120 px -> orig 10, port 18; 300 px -> orig 10, port 45. Whole-frame mean brightness follows: 300-px strip orig 2 / port 10; 16x16 grid (256 px) orig 3 / port 9. Head SPEED does scale with pixel count on both sides identically (head at 46% of the strip at t=3 s on both 60 px and 300 px), so only the tail length obeys a different law. The two laws coincide only near 60-67 px, i.e. the default rig.

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH: the original exposes NO controls at all (meta.json sides.orig.controls == []); the port adds two sliders, 'sliderSpeed' (label Speed) and 'sliderTailLength' (label TailLength). Both are live in the probe (maxDelta 17.06/53.80, maxDeltaLit 63.47/55.27) and both are value-dependent in manual sweeps.

The port's UNTOUCHED defaults already sit at the original's speed: sliderSpeed=0.25 reproduces the untouched head track exactly (heads 9,27,46 at t=1,3,5 s, same as orig), so the added speed dial does not shift the default look.

Setting sliderTailLength=0.17 (with sliderSpeed=0.25) makes the port match the original to within 5/255 per channel over a 20 s window at 10 fps (label dialed-match: meanBrightness avg 10.6 orig vs 10.8 port, motion 3.6 vs 3.6, motionLit 20.3 vs 20.0, max abs channel diff 5 at t=0/7/14/19 s). The port's tail MODEL is therefore correct; only its default length is one pixel short.
Both sides are fully deterministic and seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 produce byte-identical frames on each side (labels seed7, seed1234).
Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both), so the --sensors machinery is a no-op here.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: n/a — the original exposes no controls at all; effect unverifiable from output because the dial does not exist on that side
dials.portEffect: Live and value-dependent, but it behaves as a CYCLE TIME, not a speed: higher value = slower. Measured head rate on the 60-px strip: v=0 -> extremely fast (aliases past the dump spacing), v=0.25 -> 9.25 px/s (6.5 s per traverse, == original), v=0.5 -> 4.75 px/s (~12.6 s), v=0.75 -> 3.0 px/s (~20 s), v=1 -> 2.25 px/s (~26.7 s). Period is linear in v (~26.7 s x v); untouched default lands at v~0.24.

dials.name: sliderTailLength
dials.origEffect: n/a — control absent on the original, which draws a fixed 10-px tail at every rig size
dials.portEffect: Live and continuous. Tail length = ~2 + 58*v pixels on the 60-px rig: v=0 -> 2 px, 0.17 -> 11 px, 0.25 -> 15 px, 0.5 -> 30 px, 0.75 -> 45 px, 1 -> 60 px (whole strip lit). Untouched default is 9 px; v=0.16-0.17 reproduces the original's 10-px tail to within 4-10/255.

feedback: Default tail is one pixel short. On the default 60-px strip the original's linear fade reaches zero at tail offset 10 (per-pixel step 252/9.92 = 25.4 counts) while the port's reaches zero at offset 9 (step 28.3). Lengthen the port's default tail by one pixel; that alone closes the whole untouched gap (mean brightness 9.5 -> 10.6, max per-channel diff 25 -> ~4).

The tail length must be an ABSOLUTE pixel count, not a fraction of the strip. The original draws exactly 10 lit pixels whether the rig is 12, 60, 120, 256 or 300 pixels; the port draws 2 / 9 / 18 / 38 / 45 respectively (~15% of pixelCount). This is invisible on the default rig but very visible on real hardware with a different strip length — on a 300-px strip the port shows a 45-px rainbow smear where the original shows a tight 10-px comet, and on a 12-px strip the port shows a 2-px stub where the original lights the whole strip. Make the tail a constant 10 pixels (or make the dial's units pixels, defaulting to 10).
Head SPEED scaling is already correct — both sides traverse the strip in ~6.5 s regardless of pixel count — so do not change it while fixing the tail.

The added 'Speed' slider is inverted with respect to its label: raising it slows the snake (period ~= 26.7 s x v, so v=1 is the slowest at 26.7 s per traverse and v->0 runs away). If the dial is kept, either invert the mapping so higher = faster, or rename it to reflect that it sets cycle time. Also keep v=0 from producing an unbounded rate.

The port adds two controls the original does not have (sliderSpeed, sliderTailLength). That is an addition rather than a loss and the untouched defaults still land on the original's look, so it is acceptable — but note it as a deliberate extension. If a strict surface match is wanted, drop both and hardcode the original's 6.5 s traverse and 10-px tail.

Everything else is already exact and should not be touched: the hue-vs-head-position map, the linear fade shape, the non-wrapping tail at the strip end (fresh head at pixel 0 while the old tail decays in place at 51-59), the fps-invariant time-based motion, and long-run phase stability out to 140 s.
